title: Decision Readiness — What must be answered before choosing a route
intro: No personal facts were supplied with the request. Every row below states what is known from official sources, what is still missing, and exactly where to find it. A blank means the answer depends on your own records — not on an estimate.

known.fact: The sources reviewed describe documentation for lawful current-account income and income tax on the underlying income; they do not establish that every conversion is tax-free. SAFE also says a tax voucher is not required for qualifying current-account income that is not taxable under the rules.
known.implication: China tax and US reporting depend on the facts; a US foreign-currency gain may also require analysis.

known.fact: A foreign passport holder may buy FX with lawful China current-account income by showing ID and proof of source and amount; tax vouchers are evidence where tax applies, while SAFE says qualifying income not taxable under the rules needs no tax voucher. The cited purchase rule states no fixed cap, but does not establish that all sources qualify or guarantee a single wire.
known.implication: The cited work-pay rule does not establish the route for all sources of funds, or guarantee a single wire. Ask the bank to classify the funds and verify its limit.

known.fact: The USD 50,000 annual facilitation quota applies to domestic individuals and to holders of the Foreign Permanent Resident ID Card. A passport alone does not get the quota.
known.implication: Do not plan around a USD 50,000 cap unless you hold the PR card. The documented-income route has no stated cap.

known.fact: Rules prohibit splitting to evade limits and false documents; penalties depend on the conduct and circumstances.
known.implication: Avoid evasive or unlicensed transactions. Separate transfers are not automatically unlawful; ask the provider about its limits.

known.fact: Illustrative BOC wire: commission 1‰ (CNY 50–260), cable CNY 150, assumed full-amount delivery USD 25 and Chase incoming USD 15; the FX margin is estimated from a dated board snapshot.
known.implication: Under the stated model: {boc10k} at $10,000 and {boc400k} at $400,000. Actual costs and eligibility must be confirmed; this does not prove it is cheapest.

known.fact: Wise permits eligible non-mainland individuals with China work history and a recent China tax record to send to their own account; the provider sets an overall limit and channel-specific transfer limits.
known.implication: China bank-app transfers are limited to CNY 300,000 per transfer; other channels have different limits. Historical quotes exclude any receiving-bank fee.

known.fact: Cash: up to USD 5,000 no permit, USD 5,000–10,000 bank permit, in principle no more than USD 10,000 may be carried out. CNY cash limit CNY 20,000 per trip. US border: report over USD 10,000 on FinCEN 105.
known.implication: Cash cannot move $400,000 lawfully and must be declared at the US border.

known.fact: US citizens generally report worldwide income. A foreign tax credit may be available subject to conditions; FBAR and Form 8938 thresholds differ by circumstances.
known.implication: Foreign-currency gains and past filing obligations need individual review. Penalties depend on facts and applicable law; no personal tax or penalty can be calculated here.

known.fact: Possible China late-payment surcharges and evasion penalties were located only in excerpts; the current authoritative text and individual applicability are unverified.
known.implication: China tax collection provisions were only seen in excerpts; confirm the current law and applicability before calculating any surcharge or penalty.

known.fact: House-sale, inheritance and emigrant-property transfers have different procedures; approval requirements for a house sale remain unresolved in the sources reviewed.
known.implication: Ask the bank or SAFE to confirm the applicable route, approval requirements and documentation before assuming a wire will be accepted.

best_way.preamble: The best route cannot be ranked without the funds’ origin, eligibility, tax records and complete quotes. The following are possibilities, not a cheapest-first ranking.

routes.route: Bank of China wire (M01) — passport + source/amount evidence + tax record if applicable → buy USD at selling rate → SWIFT to your own US account, subject to the bank’s requirements and transaction limits
routes.when: Documented current-account income, subject to classification and the bank’s requirements and transaction limits.
routes.why: The model uses published fees and a dated rate; it is not an executable quote or proof that the route is cheapest.

routes.route: Wise from a China bank app or Alipay (M10) — eligibility and channel-specific limits apply.
routes.when: Eligible after-tax salary; confirm the channel-specific cap, overall limit and complete quote with Wise.
routes.why: The historical sample omits any receiving-bank fee and is not sufficient to establish the cheapest route. Ask Wise for an executable quote and confirm eligibility and limits.

routes.route: Corresponding documented route (M05/M07/M06) — sale contract + registration + tax voucher (+ SAFE approval for inheritance/emigrant)
routes.why: Procedures and taxes vary with the asset, documentation and current rules. Bank or SAFE approval requirements must be confirmed, especially for a house sale.

routes.route: Avoid evasion, false documents and unlicensed dealings (X01–X04).
routes.when: Where the proposed method would violate the applicable rules.
routes.why: Penalties vary by conduct and facts; the cited rules prohibit evasion by splitting and false documents.

questions.question: Are you a US citizen holding the account in your own name with a foreign passport, or do you hold a Foreign Permanent Resident ID Card?
questions.have_not: Whether you hold the PR card, how long you have been resident, and whether the account is solely yours. The rules treat domestic individuals, PR-card holders and passport holders differently.
questions.answer_if_known: Passport holder without PR card: use the documented-income route (no stated cap). PR-card holder: also eligible for the USD 50,000 annual quota.
questions.how_to_find: Check passport and wallet for the PR card. If resident >1 year, read FX Regulation art. 52 and SAFE Q&A 2024 with the bank.

questions.question: What is the complete source of the funds in the account — salary, bonus, housing allowance, rental income, dividends, interest, property sale, inheritance, pre-emigration assets, or a mix?
questions.have: It is CNY in a mainland bank. No source classification was supplied.
questions.have_not: Each source triggers a different lawful route and document set. Treating property proceeds as salary will be refused.
questions.answer_if_known: Salary → M01/M10. Property sale → M05. Inheritance → M07. Emigrant assets → M06. Dividends → M08. Unknown mix → cannot choose a route.
questions.how_to_find: Gather every inflow record since the account was opened: employment contracts, payslips, rental contracts, sale contracts, dividend vouchers, inheritance documents. Match each large credit to a paper trail.

questions.question: What is the exact CNY balance available to move, and in which bank and city is it held?
questions.have: User frames the decision as up to USD 400,000. No CNY balance, bank name, branch or city supplied.
questions.have_not: The CNY/USD rate and the bank's tariff decide the all-in cost. A branch in Shanghai vs. Tianjin may apply different document checks.
questions.answer_if_known: Divide CNY balance by the bank's selling rate (e.g., 6.6851 on 2026-11-10) to get the USD target. Use the cost ladder for that USD target.
questions.how_to_find: Open the bank app and export the balance and 12-month statement. Note the bank name (BOC, ICBC, HSBC etc.) and city — fees and SAFE handling differ.

questions.question: For each source of income, has China Individual Income Tax been withheld or paid, and do you have the tax payment record (完税证明) matching the amount?
questions.have: SAFE 2026 quotes Article 59 requiring source/amount evidence including tax vouchers; SAFE 2025 says a voucher is not required for qualifying current-account income not taxable under the rules. No income source or tax facts were supplied.
questions.have_not: Whether tax was due and paid, what evidence your bank accepts, and any late charges or penalties. The 2025 exception does not establish that your funds qualify or remove the need to prove source and amount; China tax collection details remain excerpt-only (F10/F11).
questions.answer_if_known: If tax was due and paid, provide the record. If qualifying current-account income is not taxable under the rules, SAFE says no tax voucher is needed, but source/amount evidence remains necessary and the bank must confirm its checklist. If tax is due but unpaid, resolve it with the tax authority before proceeding.
questions.how_to_find: Match each large credit to employment, rent, dividends, sale or inheritance records. Retrieve tax records from payroll or the tax app, determine whether tax was due, and ask the account-holding branch in writing what evidence it accepts for this source and tax treatment.

questions.question: Will the bank require the tax filing form (服务贸易等项目对外支付税务备案表) for a single payment above USD 50,000?
questions.have: STA/SAFE Announcement 2013 No. 40 lists foreign work pay above USD 50,000 per payment as needing a filing, but art. 4 sends a foreign individual's own payment to the individual FX rules.
questions.have_not: Whether your branch applies the filing to a foreign individual's own salary remittance was not confirmed. This blocks a firm $50,000+ estimate.
questions.answer_if_known: If required, file at the local tax office first, then hand the stamped form to the bank. No extra tax is stated — it is a filing.
questions.how_to_find: Call the account-holding branch and ask: 'Does a single wire above USD 50,000 for my own salary need the tax filing form?' Obtain the answer in writing or the local branch notice.

questions.question: When was each large credit earned or received, and does any remain within a use-it-or-lose-it window (e.g., CNY exchanged back within 24 months, house-sale documents)?
questions.have: Account described as 'stuck' — implies funds have accumulated.
questions.have_not: CNY converted back from foreign currency must be done within 24 months of the original exchange memo. Older property papers may need renewal.
questions.answer_if_known: Recent exchange memos → M15 within 24 months. Older funds → standard documented-income route.
questions.how_to_find: Check original exchange memos (兑回) for dates. For property, confirm the sale contract and tax voucher dates are still accepted by the bank.

questions.question: If the balance includes house-sale proceeds, inheritance or pre-emigration assets: where is the property / decedent / former hukou, and do you hold the SAFE approval for outward transfer?
questions.have: No property, inheritance or emigration facts supplied.
questions.have_not: These routes need SAFE approval from a specific branch (former hukou for emigrant, decedent's hukou for inheritance) and proof of lawful source.
questions.answer_if_known: Approved → wire directly to your own US account (not cash). No approval → bank cannot convert, even with the sale contract.
questions.how_to_find: Contact the SAFE branch of the city of former household registration or decedent's residence. Bring sale contract + registration certificate + tax vouchers (Shanghai FAQ checklist).

questions.question: What is your bank's single-wire limit, its current selling rate, and whether it charges channel discounts or requires full-amount delivery?
questions.have: Bank of China tariff and board rate verified. Other banks' rates and tariffs not verified.
questions.have_not: A bank's own channel limit may force two wires (doubling fixed fees). HSBC's margin was not published.
questions.answer_if_known: The historical BOC selling rate was 6.6911 CNY/USD at the snapshot; get a current executable quote and confirm all bank and recipient charges.
questions.how_to_find: At the branch: ask for the published tariff (服务价目表), day's selling rate, and 'single transaction maximum for outward telegraphic transfer'. Compare BOC vs. your bank at the same hour.

questions.question: Do you meet Wise's eligibility (non-mainland national, China tax record within 3 years) and does the amount fit its CNY 300,000 per-transfer cap?
questions.have: Historical Wise samples and a bank-wire scenario are available, but receiving fees and actual eligibility remain unverified; the cheapest route is unknown.
questions.have_not: Wise says its overall limit is generally based on after-tax China salary; the actual limit is set by Wise. Western Union fees and availability remain unverified.
questions.answer_if_known: Eligible and under cap → request a live Wise quote in the app at the same hour as the bank quote and compare net USD.
questions.how_to_find: Open Wise app → Send money → From CNY → verify eligibility check and per-transfer limit. Ask partner bank about WU if routing through WU.

questions.question: What is your US filing status, residency (living in US vs. abroad), and which China-source income have you already reported to the IRS?
questions.have: Stated US citizen. No filing status, residency history or prior returns supplied.
questions.have_not: Worldwide income may be taxable; foreign tax credits are conditional and foreign-currency gains may require separate analysis. Review exclusions and Form 1116 with a US tax professional.
questions.answer_if_known: Review income reporting, possible foreign-currency gain, tax credit eligibility and any prior filing failures with a US tax professional.
questions.how_to_find: Pull IRS transcripts and prior 1040s. List each China income year with CNY amount, date received, and China tax paid (for Form 1116).

questions.question: Did the aggregate of all foreign accounts exceed $10,000 at any time in the year, and did specified foreign assets exceed $50,000/$75,000 (US resident) or $200,000/$300,000 (abroad)?
questions.have: No account aggregate was supplied, but a target up to $400,000 exceeds both thresholds.
questions.have_not: Penalties are $16,536 non-willful / $165,353 willful for FBAR and $10,000–$60,000 for Form 8938. The 50%-of-balance alternative for willful FBAR was seen only pre-2016.
questions.answer_if_known: Over threshold → file FinCEN 114 by April 15 (auto to Oct 15) and Form 8938 with the return. Keep conversion and wire slips for the filing.
questions.how_to_find: Sum maximum balances of every foreign account during each calendar year. Compare to IRS comparison table.

questions.question: Has the CNY appreciated since you received it, creating a US-measured gain above $200 on the conversion?
questions.have: 26 USC 988(e)(2) ignores personal gain up to $200.
questions.have_not: Character of gain above $200 and deductibility of a loss were not verified on an IRS page.
questions.answer_if_known: At or below $200 → no gain recognized. Above $200 → give both CNY acquisition value (USD at receipt date) and conversion value to a US preparer.
questions.how_to_find: Record each receipt's date, CNY amount and USD value using the exchange rate prevailing when received (IRS foreign currency page).

questions.question: Will any portion be characterized as a gift or bequest from a nonresident alien or foreign estate exceeding $100,000 in the year?
questions.have: Form 3520 threshold is $100,000 from a nonresident alien or foreign estate.
questions.have_not: Whether funds routed through family members count as a foreign gift depends on facts not supplied.
questions.answer_if_known: Over $100,000 from those sources → file Form 3520 Part IV by the 15th day of the 4th month; penalties under 6039F(c).
questions.how_to_find: Map every sender/recipient in the chain. If a family member in China sends on your behalf, obtain the Form 3520 instructions.

questions.question: Do you need the money as cash in the US, or as a wire into a US bank account?
questions.have: Request is to convert to USD — presumably into a US account, not cash.
questions.have_not: Cash-carrying rules and declarations depend on currency, amount and circumstances; the bank’s limits for a wire are not verified.
questions.answer_if_known: For a bank balance, seek executable compliant wire quotes; cheapest and eligibility depend on the facts. For cash, check current border and declaration rules.
questions.how_to_find: Decide destination account. If cash is required, read SAFE cash rule and CBP reporting page before booking.

questions.question: Which US bank will receive the wire, and what is its incoming-wire fee and ability to accept a CNY wire?
questions.have: Chase incoming wire $15 verified. No other US bank fee was read on its own page.
questions.have_not: Some banks charge $15–$25 or cannot receive CNY. If RMB is sent and converted outside China, the receiving-bank rate was not verified.
questions.answer_if_known: Chase $15; others must be checked. If sending RMB for foreign conversion, confirm the US bank accepts CNY first.
questions.how_to_find: Ask your US bank for its 'incoming international wire fee' and 'Do you accept a CNY wire?' (for M09).

questions.question: How quickly must the funds move, and can you visit the China branch in person with original documents?
questions.have: Money described as 'stuck' — urgency not quantified.
questions.have_not: All documented bank routes require a branch visit and review. Delegating to near relatives is allowed only within limits (art. 61) and with kinship proof.
questions.answer_if_known: Can visit → proceed with M01 or property/inheritance route. Cannot visit → check delegation rules and consular authentication needs.
questions.how_to_find: Check flight/visa timeline vs. 24-month windows and annual limits (for M15 and M04).

suggestions.title: Download the account truth: 36-month statement + balance
suggestions.action: Export the bank app statement for the last 36 months as PDF. Highlight each large credit, annotate its source (salary, rent, etc.), and total the current CNY balance. Convert the CNY balance at the bank's selling rate to a USD target.
suggestions.delivers: Answers Q02 and Q03. Without this, cost estimates are hypothetical.

suggestions.title: Obtain China tax records and confirm the applicable evidence
suggestions.action: Open the Individual Income Tax app (个人所得税) or call 12366; download the tax payment record (完税证明) for each income year covering each large credit. For dividends/property, obtain the withholding slip from the payer or transfer office.
suggestions.delivers: Answers Q04. The bank will not convert without matching vouchers.

suggestions.title: Call the branch with a scripted 4-question check
suggestions.action: Ask: (a) 'For a foreign passport holder converting documented current-account income, what is my single-transaction maximum?' (b) 'Do you need the tax filing form for a single payment above USD 50,000?' (c) 'What is today's selling rate and the commission/cable/full-amount charges for one wire?' (d) 'Can a near relative handle it if I cannot visit?' Capture the answers and any notice number.
suggestions.delivers: Answers Q05, Q08, Q16. Record the call or obtain the branch notice.

suggestions.title: Classify the money into routes: salary vs. property vs. inheritance vs. other
suggestions.action: Sort each large credit into M01 (salary/current income), M05 (house sale), M07 (inheritance), M06 (pre-emigration assets), M08 (dividends) or M15 (round-tripped CNY). Anything unclassified stays unmovable until classified.
suggestions.delivers: Determines which of the 19 methods actually applies. Prevents treating property proceeds as salary.

suggestions.title: Obtain executable quotes at the same hour — bank vs. Wise vs. receiving bank
suggestions.action: At one timestamp, collect: (i) bank wire all-in estimate (FX margin + commission + cable + full-amount + receiving fee), (ii) Wise app quote for same CNY amount, (iii) US receiving-bank incoming fee. For HSBC or other mainland banks, read their own tariff and rate board at that hour.
suggestions.delivers: Answers Q08, Q09, Q15. Compare net USD credited, not headline rates. Use the cost ladder as a check, not as a quote.

suggestions.title: Reconcile US reporting before the wire moves
suggestions.action: Sum all foreign account maxima for each calendar year. Determine if FBAR ($10,000) and Form 8938 ($50k/$75k US-resident, $200k/$300k abroad) thresholds were crossed. For gifts/bequests, check Form 3520 ($100k). Obtain IRS publications and, if needed, a US preparer.
suggestions.delivers: Supports Q10–Q13; the dates of income and currency disposal can both matter.

suggestions.title: If any income was never reported or taxed, fix that before converting
suggestions.action: Engage the local tax bureau (12366) for late IIT payment and the US preparer for amended/foreign tax credit claims. Late surcharge 0.05%/day and 50%–500% fine only apply if assessed — confirm the current text on chinatax.gov.cn.
suggestions.delivers: Allows advisers to evaluate outstanding tax and reporting issues; no particular penalty can be assumed or guaranteed to be avoided.

suggestions.title: Preserve the audit trail: conversion slip + wire receipt + FBAR records
suggestions.action: Keep the stamped conversion memo, SWIFT receipt, tax vouchers, new US statement showing the credit, and annual foreign account balance records (5 years).
suggestions.delivers: Required for FBAR/8938/3520 and for any future SAFE or IRS inquiry.
